result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with continuous sidewalks on both sides but a complete lack of pedestrian-specific infrastructure like marked crossings or traffic calming. result.summary: The image shows a typical residential street with a continuous paved sidewalk separated from the roadway by a small grass buffer. While the environment is generally low-speed and residential, it lacks marked crossings and the presence of large parked vehicles creates potential sightline obstructions.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near potential crossing points or intersections to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Lighting

interventions.title: Pavement Maintenance
interventions.description: Resurface the roadway to eliminate cracks and provide a smooth surface for all users.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with row houses featuring integrated garages, resulting in frequent driveway curb cuts across the sidewalk. While sidewalks are present on both sides, they are narrow and lack a buffer from the roadway, and the visible crosswalk markings at the intersection are significantly faded.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk at the intersection is worn and barely visible, reducing driver awareness of the pedestrian crossing area.

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Conflicts
hazards.description: Numerous garage entrances create frequent points where vehicles must cross the pedestrian walkway, increasing conflict risk.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the row houses on the far side of the street

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalk Buffer
hazards.description: The narrow sidewalk is directly adjacent to the curb with no planting strip or furniture zone to separate pedestrians from traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Repaint the intersection crossing with high-visibility continental or ladder markings to improve driver compliance.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Where space permits, introduce a planting strip or street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the walkway and the road.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is poor, featuring a narrow, degraded sidewalk that is obstructed by utility poles and interrupted by a wide, unmarked driveway. There is no buffer between the walkway and the roadway, and the lack of maintenance creates tripping hazards.

hazards.name: Narrow and degraded sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk is extremely narrow and shows signs of cracking and overgrowth, making it difficult for pedestrians to navigate safely.

hazards.name: Unmarked driveway/alley crossing
hazards.description: A wide paved area for vehicle access crosses the pedestrian path without any markings or physical cues to prioritize pedestrians.

hazards.name: Utility pole obstruction
hazards.description: A large utility pole is placed directly in the narrow walking path, forcing pedestrians to step into the grass or roadway.

interventions.description: Reconstruct the sidewalk to meet ADA standards for width and surface quality, ensuring a continuous and accessible path.

interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk material across the driveway to signal pedestrian priority and slow entering/exiting vehicles.
